marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q024.takeaway: Orbicularis oculi closes eyelids and enables winking.
marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q024.displayText: The orbicularis oculi muscle plays a role in winking. It is a broad, flat, elliptical circumorbital muscle surrounding the circumference of the orbit and spreading into adjacent regions. It has orbital, palpebral and lacrimal parts and plays an important role in facial expression and ocular reflexes; it mainly closes the eyelids. It is supplied by branches of the facial, superficial temporal, maxillary and ophthalmic arteries and innervated by the temporal and zygomatic branches of the facial nerve.

rationales.a: Levator palpebrae elevates the upper eyelid and does not close it for winking.
rationales.b: Corrugator supercilii draws eyebrows medially/downward for frowning, not eyelid closure.
rationales.d: Frontalis elevates eyebrows and wrinkles forehead; orbicularis oculi closes the eyelids.

marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q025.takeaway: Great auricular nerve supplies skin over angle of mandible.
marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q025.displayText: The skin over the angle of the mandible is innervated by the great auricular nerve. Most of the skin covering the face is innervated solely by branches of the trigeminal nerve except the skin over the angle of the mandible, which is supplied by the great auricular nerve from the C2 cervical plexus, and the ear, which also receives supply from the vagus nerve, facial nerve and cervical plexus.

rationales.a: Auriculotemporal nerve supplies temporal region and part of auricle, not the angle of mandible skin territory.
rationales.b: Maxillary nerve supplies midface, not mandibular angle.
rationales.d: Facial nerve carries branchial motor fibers to facial expression, not skin sensation there.

marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q026.takeaway: Facial buccal branch innervates buccinator without piercing it; three other structures pierce it.
marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q026.displayText: The buccinator muscle is involved in flattening the cheeks against the gums and teeth; hence it is known as the whistling muscle. The buccal branch of the facial nerve innervates the buccinator muscle but does not pierce it. Structures piercing the buccinator muscle are: parotid duct; buccal branch of the mandibular nerve; and molar mucous glands which lie on the buccopharyngeal fascia around the parotid duct.

rationales.a: Parotid duct pierces buccinator to open into oral vestibule.
rationales.b: Molar mucous glands and their ducts traverse buccinator.
rationales.d: Buccal branch of mandibular nerve pierces buccinator; buccal branch of facial nerve supplies it but does not pierce it.

marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q027.takeaway: CN VI passes through Dorello canal before entering cavernous sinus.
marrow__ANAT_CH28_Q027.displayText: The abducens nerve is related to Dorello's canal. The abducens nerve enters the cavernous sinus by passing within this canal. Dorello's canal is an interdural space limited superiorly by the petrosphenoidal ligament, laterally by the petrous apex, and medially by the dorsum sellae. This is a confluence of superior petrosal, inferior petrosal, cavernous sinus and basilar plexus venous sinuses. Dorello's canal anatomy is clinically significant in understanding sixth-nerve palsy and in skull-base surgery, especially for petroclival lesions.

rationales.a: Trochlear nerve supplies superior oblique and enters orbit through superior orbital fissure, not Dorello canal.
rationales.b: Oculomotor nerve enters cavernous sinus through its roof/lateral wall and then superior orbital fissure.
rationales.d: Trigeminal nerve divisions enter cavernous sinus or skull foramina; CN VI alone traverses Dorello canal.
